questions.question: Why are output tokens typically priced higher than input tokens by most LLM providers?
options: Output tokens are always free, this is a trick question
Generating text is more computationally expensive than reading it, so output tokens are often priced several times higher than input tokens
Input tokens are actually always more expensive than output tokens
Pricing has nothing to do with computation cost
questions.explanation: Generating (producing) tokens requires more computation per token than processing (reading) input tokens, which is why providers commonly price output tokens at a higher rate than input tokens.

questions.question: Why does the cost of a single ongoing conversation tend to grow with each new turn, even if the user's new message is short?
options: Providers charge a flat fee per conversation regardless of length
Unless caching is used, each new turn re-sends the entire prior conversation history as input tokens, so input token count grows as the conversation continues
Longer conversations are always free after a certain point
This never actually happens in practice
questions.explanation: Without prefix/prompt caching, the full conversation history must be resent as input on every new turn, so token count (and therefore cost) per turn grows as a conversation gets longer.

questions.question: A team estimates a new AI feature will cost 'a few hundred dollars a month' without showing detailed numbers. Which question best pressure-tests this estimate?
options: Should we just trust this estimate and move forward?
Can you show the actual token counts (system prompt, conversation history, output length) and request volume behind this number, rather than a rough estimate?
Why do we need to know the cost at all before launching?
Can we assume the cheapest possible model without checking quality?
questions.explanation: A defensible cost estimate should be an auditable calculation based on measurable inputs (tokens per request, request volume, price per token), not a vague estimate — asking to see the actual numbers surfaces gaps before launch rather than after an unexpectedly high bill.
